item.title: Circuit compilation in the quspect quantum SDK: selecting routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis
item.description:
Read new method — quspect compiler uses 0.616 times as many two-qubit gates as Qiskit O3 (95% bootstrap interval 0.555–0.679) at 0.592 times the depth across 55 arXiv circuits on five topologies.

Grade 0.592 · 3.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Qiskit pulse: programming quantum computers through the cloud with pulses”

Figure

Geometric-mean ratios of two-qubit gate count and circuit depth relative to Qiskit O3 for 275 cases (55 circuits across five coupling topologies). Values below 1.0 indicate smaller gate counts or shallower depth than Qiskit O3.

Asks

How can circuit compilation combine layout routing and synthesis to prevent routed SWAP gates from inflating post-synthesis gate count and depth?

Before

BQSKit level 2 reached 0.853 and tket 0.930 relative to Qiskit O3 two-qubit gate counts.

But

arXiv set aggregate results informed development; loses to Qiskit on random Clifford circuits on 127- and 156-qubit devices; outputs verified numerically to 10−9 tolerance per matrix element.

Tools

coupling-constrained resynthesis · parity-state A* search · merge-aware routing large-neighborhood search · numerical three-qubit block instantiation

Code. https://github.com/QuSpect/quspect

Abstract

quspect is an open-source quantum computing SDK that provides circuit construction, C++ state-vector simulation with adjoint gradients, support for variational and combinatorial-optimization algorithms, Hamiltonian simulation, control-pulse envelopes and backends for several cloud quantum processors. Here we describe and evaluate its circuit compiler. Routing and synthesis interact: inserting a SWAP can change the circuit structure that later optimization exploits. At its highest optimization level, the compiler evaluates a screened set of routing candidates by their cost after coupling-constrained resynthesis. The pipeline combines parity-state A* search for small CNOT-phase regions, heuristic synthesis for larger regions, and numerical three-qubit instantiation with a per-block 10^-9 check. For a fixed phase polynomial, A* certifies the minimum CX count when it reaches a goal within budget. On an evaluation set of 55 circuits from 41 arXiv papers on five topologies, the compiler uses 0.616 times as many two-qubit gates as Qiskit O3 (95% circuit-cluster bootstrap interval 0.555-0.679) at 0.592 times its depth. BQSKit level 2 reaches 0.853 and tket 0.930. On a 17-qubit superconducting processor, the compiled circuits had the fewest CZ gates in all six scenarios of the main run. Ablations assess the contributions within the integrated pipeline.

item.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
item.description:
Read new method — GNN-based region scoring CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the best baseline across 324 quantum circuits on the TianYan-176 processor. Reusing the trained model with updated calibration data preserves the highest mean fidelity across six dates without retraining.

Grade 0.503 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Noise-Adaptive Compiler Mappings for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Computers” · Wenjie Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Zhigang Wang, Yuchen He, Shengbin Wang, Hantao Sun

Figure

Bar chart comparing the mean measurement-distribution fidelity across seven benchmark datasets for CREST and four baseline methods on TianYan-176.

Asks

How can quantum compilation select execution subregions on superconducting processors to optimize circuit-specific execution fidelity while remaining robust across recalibrations without retraining?

Before

Baseline compilation methods QSteed, SABRE, and HAQA. On the 96 held-out circuit benchmark, mean fidelity was 0.18100 (HAQA) versus 0.21347 with CREST.

But

Evaluated on a single superconducting device architecture (TianYan-176) across circuits up to 20 qubits; offline candidate graph precomputation required.

Tools

Graph neural network (GNN) scoring · Bidirectional cross-graph attention · TianYan-176 superconducting processor · Multiscale candidate region construction

Abstract

Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. It encodes gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions alongside each candidate region's connectivity and current calibration attributes; bidirectional cross-graph attention relates the two representations, while real-device execution outcomes supervise candidate ranking. The trained scorer is reused with updated calibration attributes. Evaluations on 324 circuits from seven datasets on TianYan-176 show that CREST improves mean measurement-distribution fidelity by 19.03% over the strongest baseline and achieves the highest mean fidelity on every dataset. Furthermore, using updated calibration attributes, the same trained model maintains the highest overall mean fidelity across six measurement dates without retraining. With a unified model of circuit-region compatibility, CREST improves execution fidelity across diverse workloads and sustains that advantage as hardware calibration changes.

arxave:action.title: Adapt CREST region scorer to spin-qubit calibration data

item.arxave:action: Implement the circuit-region compatibility scorer using the team's spin-qubit connectivity and calibration attributes (T1/T2, 1Q/2Q error, readout fidelity) and benchmark it against the current transpiler on 16-qubit workloads.

arxave:action.title: Test calibration-drift robustness on spin-qubit snapshots

item.arxave:action: Collect calibration snapshots over several weeks and verify whether a trained scorer retains its fidelity advantage without retraining, as claimed for six measurement dates on TianYan-176.

arxave:action.title: Ask authors about small-device and sparse-connectivity behavior

item.arxave:action: CREST was evaluated on a 176-qubit superconducting chip; ask how candidate-region construction and GNN scoring perform on 16-50 qubit spin-qubit arrays with sparse nearest-neighbour connectivity.

arxave:action.title: Training labels require real-device execution outcomes

item.arxave:action: CREST supervises candidate ranking with real-device execution fidelity; on the spin-qubit machine this requires a data-collection pipeline and may be expensive, so plan a bootstrapping strategy using simulation or limited hardware runs.
